For iQIYI's annual English-region user research, Hengzhen built a framework connecting content preference, audience segmentation, and growth pathways, then analyzed 33,876 completed responses in Python across content interests, membership status, age, country, and discovery channels.

Compared awareness, viewing interest, and preference across Asian dramas, short-form dramas, animation, and AI content. Content does not play a single role in growth: Chinese dramas form a consumption base, BL/GL resonates with younger members, Korean dramas and animation show stronger acquisition potential.
Cross-analyzed country, age, membership status, and ethnicity to find where the same content carries different value.
Short-form drama is discovered more often through social media. For non-users, social channels are the opening to create discovery and guide interest toward iQIYI.

Telling spam tokens from real ones
Ethereum Token Fraud Detection · Team research project, Duke University

For Ethereum tokens that imitate the symbols of verified assets, the team built a behavioral classification prototype. It analyzes roughly 2.2M transfer events to compare risk patterns across token contracts.
Spam tokens cluster in a narrow block window and show concentrated distribution. 34.0% of spam tokens were active in only one block, against 7.2% of legitimate tokens.

Engineered 27 behavioral features over 3,606 labeled tokens and benchmarked six classifiers. Symbol collisions were used to construct labels, not as model inputs, so the classifier learned on-chain behavior rather than the labeling rule. LightGBM tuned with five-fold cross-validation reached 0.89 macro F1, 0.96 AUC, and a 90% fraud-detection rate.
Semi-supervised expansion with about 8,750 unlabeled tokens did not improve performance. Distribution shift and pseudo-label noise made the supervised model more reliable.

Applied SHAP to surface fraud signals such as short active windows and concentrated senders, translating them into risk-control rules and a business-cost-aware decision threshold. Contributed across framing, label construction, feature engineering, model comparison, and interpretation.
Rather than token names, the model relied most on activity spread, transfer value, and sender concentration.
